texts.li: A crew of woodcutters from {FACTION} has come to the woods {PLACE}, axes on their shoulders and a pack beast behind. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they cut for the towns of the region and would camp a few days by the colony's trees, cutting what they can carry and keeping to their side.

[their:tribal] Wood-gatherers of {FACTION} have come out of the hills to the woods {PLACE}, with a beast to drag the logs home. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might take wood from the colony's side of the hills for a few days, as their people have always taken it.

[their:medieval] Woodcutters of {FACTION} have come to the woods {PLACE} with their axes and a pack beast. {X_nameDef}, their foreman, asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp and cut for a few days. They will fell only what they can carry, {X_pronoun} says, and keep clear of the colony's fields.

[their:industrial] A logging crew of {FACTION} has come to the woods {PLACE} with a pack beast for the timber. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, cap in hand, whether they might work the trees there for a few days. Timber is wanted down the road, and these are good trees.

settled.li: [shelter:hut] The woodcutters' camp {PLACE} is up: a fire, and a hut of logs between it and the wind.
The woodcutters' camp {PLACE} is up: a fire, and their axes laid out ready.
The woodcutters from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}. The pack beast is tethered, and the crew are already looking over the trees.
[shelter:hut] At the woodcutters' camp {PLACE}, a hut of fresh logs stands by the fire.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the youngest of the woodcutters {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} has cut enough of other people's trees, and asks whether the colony could use a strong back and a good eye for timber.
{X_nameDef} from the woodcutters' camp has asked whether there might be a place for {X_objective} at the colony, where the trees stay standing and the fire is somebody else's to keep.

farewell.li: The woodcutters from {FACTION} have gone on, their pack beast loaded to the ears.
The woodcutters' camp {PLACE} is gone, the fire raked out and the stumps left behind.
{X_nameDef} and the crew have gone off down the road, and the woods {PLACE} are quiet again.

li.label: Buy a load of their wood ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the woodcutters carries a load of their wood to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver, counted it once, and sent one of the crew off with a load for the colony's gate.
The woodcutters will carry a load of their wood to the colony's gate today. {X_nameDef} says it's dry enough to burn by winter.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn the axe from them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} works a few hours beside the woodcutters, learning where to cut and how a tree falls. Practice at growing and plant work.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is out with the woodcutters today, learning from {X_nameDef} where to cut so a tree falls where it's meant to.
{X_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} out to the trees to show {A_objective} the woodcutter's way of reading a trunk.

li.label: Send a hot supper over to the crew

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} came up from the woodcutters' camp {PLACE} at the end of the day, stiff and smelling of resin. The crew have been living on hard bread since they came, and would give a lot for a hot supper from the colony's kitchen.

[their:tribal] {X_nameDef} of the wood-gatherers came to the colony's gate at dusk and asked, without much hope, whether the colony had cooked food to spare for the people who have been cutting all day.

li.tip: Four of the colony's meals are carried out to the woodcutters' camp.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is carrying four hot meals down to the woodcutters' camp, and {X_nameDef} has gone back to tell the crew.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} nodded and went back to the camp, where the crew had another night of hard bread.

li.label: a hot supper for the woodcutters

titles.li: [their:spacer] A survey of the land's plants

texts.li: Herb-gatherers of {FACTION} have come along the road with baskets and a pack beast, looking for the plants that heal. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they go where the wild herbs grow thick, and asked to camp {PLACE} a few days and gather.

[their:tribal] Root-diggers of {FACTION} have come down with digging sticks and baskets on their backs. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the land here grows roots their healers need, and asked to camp {PLACE} and dig for a few days.

[their:medieval] Herbalists of {FACTION} have come up the track with a pack beast and a dozen baskets. {X_nameDef}, the eldest, asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} and gather on the colony's wild ground for a few days. They will leave the colony a share, {X_pronoun} says, as is right.

[their:industrial] A botanist of {FACTION} and students have arrived with a pack beast and their notebooks. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days to collect the land's medicinal plants.

[their:spacer] A small survey party of {FACTION} has come to catalogue the land's plants, with a pack beast for their gear. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} and gather for a few days.

settled.li: The herb-gatherers' camp {PLACE} is up: a table under the trees covered in bundles drying, and a fire kept low so the smoke doesn't get into them.
The herb-gatherers from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}. The pack beast grazes, and their table is already covered in leaves and roots.
At the herb-gatherers' camp {PLACE}, bundles of something green are drying on their table in the sun.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the youngest of the herb-gatherers {PLACE}, says the colony's wild ground is the best {X_pronoun} has seen in years, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay and tend it.
{X_nameDef} of the herb-gatherers asked {A_nameDef} whether the colony's healer could use a pair of hands that knows which leaf is which.

farewell.li: The herb-gatherers from {FACTION} have gone on with their baskets full and the pack beast complaining under them.
The herb-gatherers' camp {PLACE} is empty this morning. They left at dawn, gathering as they went.
{X_nameDef} thanked the colony for the use of its wild ground and led the herb-gatherers off down the road, stopping twice before the edge to dig.

lines.li: Leave the roots, take the leaves.
Never take the last of a patch.

helpTexts.li: [medicine] {X_nameDef} of the herb-gatherers went out at dawn and came back with more than they need. {COUNT} bundles of herbal medicine are waiting on the colony's side of their camp.

li.label: Buy a few bundles of their herbs ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the herb-gatherers carries a few bundles of herbal medicine to the colony's gate.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver and picked out the best of the bundles. One of them is carrying them over to the colony's gate.
The herb-gatherers will carry a few bundles over to the colony's gate today, tied in grass, the best they have.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn the herbs with them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends a few hours at the herb-gatherers' side, learning what heals and what harms. Practice in medicine.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is out with the herb-gatherers today, learning from {X_nameDef} what heals and what harms.
{X_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} along on the gathering, to show {A_objective} which leaf is for a fever and which one only looks like it.

li.label: Let them walk the colony's fields
li.refuseLabel: Keep them out of the fields

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} asks whether the herb-gatherers might walk the colony's fields. The herbs they want often grow at the edges of a crop, {X_pronoun} says, and they would touch nothing that's the colony's, and leave a share of what they find.

[their:medieval] The eldest of the herbalists asked {A_nameDef}, very politely, whether they might walk the colony's field edges, where the useful weeds grow. A share of the gathering would be the colony's, as is right.

li.tip: Two of the herb-gatherers walk the colony's fields for a couple of hours, and their healer gathers herbs at the next dawn and leaves a share for the colony.

outcomes.li: Two of the herb-gatherers will walk the colony's fields today, looking for the herbs that grow among the crops.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} said the wild ground was plenty, and the herb-gatherers kept to it.

lines.li: Here, at the edge of the row.
